questions_and_answers.question_text: What does the question with completion le ask?
What does the question with combined le ask?
What is the negative answer with completion le?
What is the negative answer with combined le?
Write the Chinese for "No, he didn't come."
How is the SAME question Tā lái le ma? interpreted in the two cases?

answers.answer_text: With completion le it means "Did he come?"; with combined le it means "Has he come?"

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which negative adverb is used to negate completion le?
Does the marker le appear in the negative answer?

answers.answer_text: No — the negative of Tā lái le is Tā méi lái, with no le.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Yes, he came."
Which of the two questions asks whether the resulting new situation still exists?

articles.text:
9. A: Tā lái le ma?                         Did he come?
   B: Lái le, tā lái le.                    Yes, he came.

10. A: Tā lái le ma?                        Did he come?
    B: Méi lái, tā méi lái.                 No, he didn't come.

Notes on Nos. 9-10

Compare the two possible interpretations of the question Tā lái le ma? and the answers they receive:

Completion le
Tā  | lái le ma?          (Did he come?)
Tā  | lái le.             (He came.)
Tā  | méi lái.            (He didn't come.)

Combined le
Tā  | lái le ma?          (Has he come?)
Tā  | lái le.             (He has come.)
Tā  | hái méi lái.        (He hasn't come yet.)

The first question, with completion le, asks only if the action took place. The second question, with combined le, asks both whether the action has been completed and whether the resulting new situation still exists.
